o1.biggest_strength: It correctly rebuilds the flow around the strongest signal in the data: bring back pause for 'no time' and stop wasting discounts on people likely to return anyway.
o1.biggest_mistake: It uses weak placeholder assumptions for the annual-switch and reminder offers, so some projected lift beyond the pause is less well supported than the headline suggests.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the forecast by separating proven lift from assumed lift more clearly and add a simple build order with must-have versus test-next items.

o2.biggest_strength: It keeps the flow simple and mostly respects the brand voice and one-save-screen rule.
o2.biggest_mistake: It reintroduces 50% off for 'switching apps' without evidence, which goes against the margin signal in the brief and weakens the money logic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unsupported discount, keep the strongest reason-based saves only, and recast the forecast using only proven data or clearly bounded test assumptions.

reason: Output 1 is the one I could hand to product next sprint: it follows the data, avoids wasting discounts, and gives me usable copy plus sensible economics. Output 2 is dragged down by an unsupported discount choice and shakier money logic.
